To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DU process in the hadronic star layer and the Vela mass problem can be explained by the presence of a color superconductivity phase transition to the quark matter state.

(i) the TA data are consistent with a mass distribution which is narrower than the population synthesis one; (ii) the DU process in the hadronic star is not excluded by the TA data, however, it requires a mass distribution which does not overlap with the one for young NSs; and (iii) the Vela mass problem can be solved in a natural manner if a color superconductivity with a density dependent diquark pairing is assumed

(i) the mass distribution of NSs can be used to constrain the composition of the NS interior, (ii) the mass distribution can be extracted from the TA diagram, (iii) a satisfactory agreement with the data can be achieved by hybrid stars with color superconducting cores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the composition of neutron stars, which is one of the key issues of modern nuclear astrophysics.
a systematic analysis of the cooling of NSs and the extraction of constraints on the composition of the stellar interior.
the question how the statistics of NS masses can be used to constrain NS cooling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NS cooling data and the mass distribution of young NSs are not compatible with the EoS of the hadronic phase of the matter, but are consistent with the EoS for hybrid stars.
the NS mass distribution is a powerful tool to constrain the composition of the NS interior.
a hybrid star model can explain both the TA data and the mass distribution of NSs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass distribution of NSs in combination with cooling simulations can be a powerful tool for constraining the EoS at high densities.
the TA data and the population synthesis mass distribution are in conflict with each other and with the EoS of pure hadronic stars.
the mass distributions of the NS populations are a powerful tool in constraining the NS interiors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mass distribution of NSs is a powerful tool to constrain the EoS of dense matter.
the mass distributions of young and nearby NSs can be used as a powerful tool for constraining the composition of NS interiors.
the TA data and the mass distribution of NSs are intimately related and can be used to constrain EoSs.
